    and their hope will be as the giving up of breath.”
Job 12:2:
“no doubt but you are the people,
    and wisdom will die with you!
Job 12:5:
he whose foot is unsteady
    is despised in the thoughts of him who is at ease.
Job 12:6:
the tents of robbers are at peace,
    and those who provoke god are secure,
    into whose hand they bring their own god.
Job 12:7:
“but now ask the beasts, and let them teach you;
    and the birds of the air, and let them tell you;
Job 12:8:
or speak to the earth, let it teach you;
    and let the fish of the sea declare to you.
Job 12:9:
who among all these does not know
    that the hand of the lord has done this,
Job 12:10:
in whose hand is the soul of every living thing
    and the breath of all mankind?
Job 12:11:
does not the ear test words
    and the mouth taste its food?
Job 12:12:
wisdom is with the elderly,
    and understanding comes with long life.
Job 12:13:
“with him are wisdom and strength;
    he has counsel and understanding.
Job 12:14:
surely, he tears down, and it cannot be built again;
    he imprisons a man, and there can be no release.
Job 12:15:
surely, he withholds the waters, and they dry up;
    also he sends them out, and they overthrow the earth.
Job 12:16:
with him are strength and wisdom.
    the deceived and the deceiver are his.
Job 12:17:
he leads counselors away stripped
    and makes fools of judges.
Job 12:18:
he has loosened the bonds imposed by kings
    and bound their waist with a belt.
Job 12:19:
he leads away priests stripped
    and overthrows the mighty.
Job 12:20:
he removes speech from the trusted ones
    and takes away the understanding of the aged.
Job 12:21:
he pours contempt upon princes
    and loosens the belt of the mighty.
Job 12:22:
he uncovers deep things out of darkness
    and brings the shadow of death to light.
Job 12:23:
he increases the nations and destroys them;
    he enlarges the nations and guides them.
Job 12:24:
he takes away the understanding of the chiefs of the people of the earth,
    and causes them to wander in a wilderness where there is no way.
Job 12:25:
they grope in the dark without light,
    and he makes them to stagger like a drunk man.
Job 13:1:
“notice, my eye has seen all this;
    my ear has heard and understood it.
Job 13:2:
what you know, i also know the same;
    i am not inferior to you.
Job 13:3:
surely i would speak to the almighty,
    and i desire to reason with god.
Job 13:4:
but you are plasterers of falsehood;
    you are all physicians of no value.
Job 13:5:
oh, that you would altogether hold your peace,
    and it would be your wisdom!
Job 13:6:
hear now my reasoning,
    and listen to the pleadings of my lips.
Job 13:7:
will you speak wickedly for god?
    and talk deceitfully for him?
Job 13:8:
will you take his side?
    will you plead for god?
Job 13:9:
is it good that he would search you out?
    or as one man mocks another, do you so mock him?
Job 13:10:
he will surely rebuke you,
    if you secretly show partiality.
Job 13:11:
will not his excellence make you afraid,
    and the dread of him fall upon you?
Job 13:12:
your reminders are parables made of ashes;
    your answers are answers made of clay.
Job 13:13:
“hold your peace; leave me alone, that i may speak,
    and let come on me what may!
Job 13:14:
why do i take my flesh in my teeth
    and put my life in my hand?
Job 13:15:
though he slay me, yet will i trust in him,
    but i will defend my own ways before him.
Job 13:16:
he also will be my salvation,
    for a hypocrite could not come before him.
Job 13:17:
listen carefully to my speech,
    and to my declaration with your ears.
Job 13:18:
see now, i have prepared my case;
    i know that i will be justified.
Job 13:19:
who is he who will plead with me?
    for now, if i hold my tongue, i will give up my breath.
Job 13:20:
“only grant me two things,
    then i will not hide myself from you:
Job 13:21:
withdraw your hand far from me,
    and let not the dread of you make me afraid.
Job 13:22:
then call, and i will answer;
    or let me speak, and you answer me.
Job 13:23:
how many are my iniquities and sins?
    make known to me my transgression and my sin.
Job 13:24:
why do you hide your face
    and regard me as your enemy?
Job 13:25:
will you frighten a leaf driven to and fro?
    and will you pursue dry stubble?
Job 13:26:
for you write bitter things against me
    and make me inherit the iniquities of my youth.
Job 13:28:
“man, as a rotten thing, decays,
    as a garment that is moth eaten.
Job 14:1:
“man who is born of a woman
    is of few days and full of trouble.
Job 14:2:
he comes forth like a flower and withers;
    he flees like a shadow and does not continue.
Job 14:3:
do you open your eyes on such a one,
    and bring me into judgment with you?
Job 14:4:
who can bring a clean thing out of an unclean?
    there is no one.
Job 14:6:
turn from him, that he may rest,
    until he, as a hired man, finishes his day.
Job 14:8:
though its root may grow old in the earth,
    and its stump may die in the ground,
Job 14:9:
yet at the scent of water it will bud
    and bring forth boughs like a plant.
Job 14:10:
but man dies and wastes away;
    yes, man gives up his breath, and where is he?
Job 14:11:
as the waters disappear from the sea,
    and the flood shrivels and dries up,
Job 14:13:
“oh, that you would hide me in the grave,
    that you would conceal me until your wrath is past,
that you would appoint me a set time
    and remember me!
Job 14:14:
if a man dies, will he live again?
    all the days of my service i will wait,
    until my relief comes.
Job 14:15:
you will call, and i will answer you;
    you will long for the work of your hands.
Job 14:16:
for now you number my steps;
    do you not observe my sin?
Job 14:17:
my transgression is sealed up in a bag,
    and you plaster over my iniquity.
Job 14:18:
“surely the mountain falling comes to nothing,
    and the rock is removed out of its place.
Job 14:20:
you prevail forever against him, and he passes on;
    changing his countenance, you send him away.
Job 14:21:
his sons come to honor, and he does not know it;
    and they are brought low, but he does not perceive it.
Job 14:22:
but his flesh on him will have pain,
    and his soul within him will mourn.”
Job 15:2:
“should a wise man reply with empty knowledge
    and fill his lungs with the east wind?
Job 15:3:
should he reason with unprofitable talk
    or with speeches with which he can do no good?
Job 15:4:
yes, you cast off reverence
    and hinder prayer before god.
Job 15:5:
for your mouth utters your iniquity,
    and you choose the tongue of the crafty.
Job 15:6:
your own mouth condemns you, and not i;
    yes, your own lips testify against you.
Job 15:7:
“are you the first man who was born?
    or were you made before the hills?
Job 15:8:
have you heard the counsel of god?
    and do you restrict wisdom to yourself?
Job 15:9:
what do you know that we do not know?
    what do you understand that is not in us?
Job 15:10:
both the gray-haired and very aged are among us—
    much older than your father.
Job 15:11:
are the consolations of god too small for you?
    or the word spoken gently to you?
Job 15:12:
why does your heart carry you away?
    and what do your eyes wink at,
Job 15:13:
that you turn your spirit against god,
    and let such words go out of your mouth?
Job 15:14:
“what is man that he should be pure?
    and he who is born of a woman, that he should be righteous?
Job 15:15:
behold, he puts no trust in his holy ones,
    and the heavens are not pure in his sight.
Job 15:16:
how much more abhorred and corrupt is man,
    who drinks iniquity like water!
Job 15:17:
“i will tell you; hear me,
    and what i have seen i will declare,
Job 15:18:
what wise men have told,
    not hiding anything received from their fathers,
Job 15:19:
to whom alone the land was given,
    and no foreigner passed among them:
Job 15:20:
the wicked man travails with pain all his days,
    and numbered are the years stored up for the oppressor.
Job 15:21:
a dreadful sound is in his ears;
    in prosperity the destroyer will come upon him.
Job 15:22:
he does not believe that he will return from darkness,
    and a sword awaits him.
Job 15:23:
he wanders about for bread, saying, ‘where is it?’
    he knows that the day of darkness is ready at his hand.
Job 15:24:
trouble and anguish will make him afraid;
    they will prevail against him as a king ready to the battle.
Job 15:25:
for he stretches out his hand against god,
    and strengthens himself against the almighty.
Job 15:26:
he rushes upon him, even on his neck,
    with his thick embossed shield.
Job 15:27:
“he has covered his face with his fatness
    and gathered fat upon his waist.
Job 15:28:
he dwells in desolate cities
    and in houses which no man inhabits,
    which are ready to become heaps.
Job 15:29:
he will not be rich, nor will his wealth continue,
    nor will his possessions spread over the earth.
Job 15:31:
let him who is deceived not trust in futility,
    for futility will be his reward.
Job 15:32:
it will be accomplished before his time,
    and his branch will not be green.
Job 15:33:
he will shake off his unripe grape like the vine,
    and will cast off his blossom like the olive.
Job 15:34:
for the company of hypocrites will be desolate,
    and fire will consume the tents of bribery.
Job 15:35:
they conceive mischief, and give birth to futility;
    their womb prepares deceit.”
Job 16:2:
“i have heard many such things;
    miserable comforters are you all!
Job 16:3:
will windy words have an end?
    or what provokes you that you answer?
Job 16:4:
i also could speak as you do,
    if your soul were in my place.
i could heap up words against you
    and shake my head at you;
Job 16:5:
but i would strengthen you with my mouth,
    and the moving of my lips would relieve your grief.
Job 16:6:
“though i speak, my grief is not relieved;
    and though i stop, how am i eased?
Job 16:7:
but now he has made me weary;
    you have made desolate all my company.
Job 16:8:
you have filled me with wrinkles, which is a witness against me;
    and my leanness has risen up and bears witness to my face.
Job 16:11:
god has delivered me to the ungodly
    and turned me over into the hands of the wicked.
Job 16:12:
i was at ease, but he has shattered me.
    he also has taken me by my neck, and shaken me to pieces,
and set me up for his target.
Job 16:14:
he pierces me with thrust after thrust;
    he rushes upon me like a warrior.
Job 16:15:
“i have sewn sackcloth over my skin
    and thrust my horn into the dust.
Job 16:16:
my face is inflamed with weeping,
    and on my eyelids is the shadow of death,
Job 16:17:
though not for any violence in my hands,
    and my prayer is pure.
Job 16:18:
“o earth, do not cover my blood,
    and let my cry have no resting place.
Job 16:19:
also now, look, my witness is in heaven,
    and my record is on high.
Job 16:20:
my friends scorn me;
    my eyes pour out tears unto god.
Job 16:21:
oh, that one might plead for a man with god,
    as a man pleads for his neighbor!
Job 16:22:
“for when a few years have passed,
    i will go the way from which i will not return.
Job 17:1:
“my spirit is broken,
    my days are extinguished,
    the grave is ready for me.
Job 17:2:
are not mockers with me?
    and does not my eye dwell on their provocation?
Job 17:3:
“now put down a pledge for me with yourself.
    who is he who will shake hands with me?
Job 17:4:
for you have hidden their heart from understanding.
    therefore will you not exalt them.
Job 17:5:
he who speaks flattery to his friends,
    even the eyes of his children will fail.
Job 17:6:
“and he has made me a byword of the people,
    someone in whose face they spit.
Job 17:7:
my eye also is dim because of sorrow,
    and all my members are like a shadow.
Job 17:8:
upright men will be astonished at this,
    and the innocent will stir up himself against the hypocrite.
Job 17:9:
the righteous also will hold to his way,
    and he who has clean hands will be stronger and stronger.
Job 17:10:
“but as for you all, return and come now,
    for i cannot find one wise man among you.
Job 17:11:
my days are past, my purposes are broken off,
    even the thoughts of my heart.
Job 17:12:
they change the night into day;
    the light is short because of darkness.
Job 17:13:
if i wait, the grave is my house;
    i have made my bed in the darkness.
Job 17:14:
i have said to the pit, ‘you are my father’;
    to the worm, ‘you are my mother and my sister.’
Job 17:15:
where now is my hope?
    as for my hope, who will see it?
Job 17:16:
will they go down to the gates of sheol?
    will we descend together in the dust?”
Job 18:2:
“how long will it be until you put an end to words?
    gain understanding, and afterwards we will speak.
Job 18:3:
why are we counted as beasts
    and regarded as stupid in your sight?
Job 18:4:
you who tear yourself in anger,
    will the earth be forsaken for you?
    and will the rock be removed from its place?
Job 18:5:
“yes, the light of the wicked will be put out,
    and the spark of his fire will not shine.
Job 18:6:
the light will be dark in his tent,
    and his candle beside him will be put out.
Job 18:7:
the steps of his strength will be shortened,
    and his own counsel will cast him down.
Job 18:8:
for he is cast into a net by his own feet,
    and he walks upon a snare.
Job 18:9:
the trap will take him by the heel,
    and the snare will prevail against him.
Job 18:10:
the snare is laid for him in the ground,
    and a trap for him in the path.
Job 18:11:
terrors will make him afraid on every side
    and will drive him to his feet.
Job 18:12:
his strength will be hungry,
    and destruction will be ready at his side.
Job 18:13:
it will devour the parts of his skin;
    the firstborn of death will devour his limbs.
Job 18:14:
his confidence will be rooted out of his tent,
    and it will bring him to the king of terrors.
Job 18:15:
they dwell in his tent who have no part with him;
    brimstone will be scattered upon his habitation.
Job 18:16:
his roots will be dried up beneath,
    and above his branch will dry up.
Job 18:17:
the memory of him will perish from the earth,
    and he will have no name in the street.
Job 18:18:
he will be driven from light into darkness,
    and chased out of the world.
Job 18:19:
he has neither descendant nor posterity among his people,
    nor anyone remaining in his dwellings.
Job 18:20:
they who come after him will be astonished at his day,
    as they who went before were seized with fright.
Job 18:21:
surely such are the dwellings of the wicked,
    and this is the place of him who does not know god.”
Job 19:2:
“how long will you torment my soul
    and break me in pieces with words?
Job 19:3:
these ten times you have reproached me;
    you are not ashamed that you have wronged me.
Job 19:4:
and if indeed i have erred,
    my error remains with me.
Job 19:5:
if indeed you exalt yourselves against me
    and plead against me with my disgrace,
Job 19:6:
know now that god has bent me
    and has surrounded me with his net.
Job 19:7:
“look, i cry out concerning wrong, but i am not heard;
    i cry aloud, but there is no justice.
Job 19:8:
he has fenced up my way that i cannot pass,
    and he has set darkness in my paths.
Job 19:9:
he has stripped me of my glory
    and taken the crown from my head.
Job 19:10:
he has destroyed me on every side, and i am gone;
    my hope he has uprooted like a tree.
Job 19:11:
he has also kindled his wrath against me,
    and he counts me as one of his enemies.
Job 19:13:
“he has removed my brothers far from me,
    and my acquaintances are completely estranged from me.
Job 19:14:
my relatives have failed,
    and my close friends have forgotten me.
Job 19:16:
i called my servant, but he gave me no answer;
    i begged him with my mouth.
Job 19:17:
my breath is offensive to my wife;
    i am loathsome to the children of my own body.
Job 19:18:
yes, young children despise me;
    i arose, and they spoke against me.
Job 19:19:
all my close friends abhorred me,
    and they whom i love are turned against me.
Job 19:20:
my bones cling to my skin and to my flesh,
    and i have escaped by the skin of my teeth.
Job 19:21:
“have pity upon me, have pity upon me, o you my friends,
    for the hand of god has struck me!
Job 19:22:
why do you persecute me as god does,
    and are not satisfied with my flesh?
Job 19:23:
“oh, that my words were written!
    oh, that they were inscribed in a book!
Job 19:24:
that they were engraved with an iron pen
    and lead in the rock forever!
Job 19:25:
for i know that my redeemer lives,
    and he will stand at last on the earth;
Job 19:26:
and after my skin is destroyed,
    yet in my flesh i will see god,
Job 19:27:
whom i will see for myself,
    and my eyes will behold, and not another.
    how my heart yearns within me.
Job 19:28:
“if you should say, ‘how shall we persecute him?’
    since the root of the matter is found in me,
Job 20:2:
“therefore my thoughts cause me to answer,
    and for this i make haste.
Job 20:3:
i have heard the rebuke that disgraces me,
    and the spirit of my understanding causes me to answer.
Job 20:4:
“do you not know this of old,
    since man was placed upon earth,
Job 20:5:
that the triumphing of the wicked is short,
    and the joy of the hypocrite is but for a moment?
Job 20:6:
though his loftiness extends to the heavens,
    and his head reaches to the clouds,
Job 20:7:
yet he will perish forever like his own excrement;
    those who have seen him will say, ‘where is he?’
Job 20:8:
he will fly away like a dream and will not be found;
    yes, he will be chased away as a vision of the night.
Job 20:9:
the eye that saw him will see him no more;
    nor will his place behold him anymore.
Job 20:10:
his children will seek favor from the poor,
    and his hands will give back his wealth.
Job 20:11:
his bones are full of his youthful vigor,
    but it will lie down with him in the dust.
Job 20:12:
“though evil is sweet in his mouth,
    and he hides it under his tongue,
Job 20:13:
though he spares it and does not forsake it,
    but keeps it in his mouth,
Job 20:14:
yet his food in his stomach turns sour;
    it becomes the venom of cobras within him.
Job 20:16:
he will suck the poison of cobras;
    the viper’s tongue will slay him.
Job 20:17:
he will not see the streams, the rivers,
    the brooks of honey and butter.
Job 20:18:
he will give back the produce of labor and will not swallow it down.
    according to his wealth the restitution will be, and he will not rejoice in it;
Job 20:19:
because he has oppressed and has forsaken the poor.
    he has violently taken away a house that he did not build.
Job 20:20:
“because he knows no quietness in his belly,
    he will not save anything he desired.
Job 20:21:
nothing is left for him to eat;
    therefore his prosperity will not endure.
Job 20:22:
in his self-sufficiency he will be in distress;
    every hand of misery will come upon him.
Job 20:23:
when he is about to fill his belly,
    god will cast the fury of his wrath on him
    and will rain it on him while he is eating.
Job 20:24:
he will flee from the iron weapon;
    a bronze bow will pierce him through.
Job 20:27:
the heavens will reveal his iniquity,
    and the earth will rise up against him.
Job 20:28:
the increase of his house will depart,
    and his goods will flow away in the day of his wrath.
Job 20:29:
this is the wicked man’s portion from god,
    and the inheritance appointed to him by god.”
Job 21:2:
“listen carefully to my speech,
    and let this be your consolation.
Job 21:3:
bear with me that i may speak,
    and after i have spoken, mock on.
Job 21:4:
“as for me, is my complaint against man?
    and if it were so, why should not my spirit be troubled?
Job 21:5:
look at me and be astonished,
    and put your hand over your mouth.
Job 21:6:
even when i remember i am afraid,
    and trembling takes hold of my body.
Job 21:7:
why do the wicked live and become old;
    yes, become mighty in power?
Job 21:8:
their descendants are established with them in their sight,
    and their offspring before their eyes.
Job 21:9:
their houses are safe from fear,
    nor is the rod of god upon them.
Job 21:10:
their bull breeds without failure;
    their cow gives calves without miscarriage.
Job 21:11:
they send forth their little ones like a flock,
    and their children dance.
Job 21:12:
they take up the tambourine and harp
    and rejoice at the sound of the flute.
Job 21:13:
they spend their days in wealth,
    and in a moment go down to sheol.
Job 21:14:
therefore they say to god, ‘depart from us,
    for we do not desire the knowledge of your ways.
Job 21:15:
who is the almighty, that we should serve him?
    and what profit do we have if we pray to him?’
Job 21:16:
indeed, their prosperity is not in their hand.
    the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
Job 21:17:
“how often is the lamp of the wicked put out?
    how often does their destruction come upon them,
    the sorrows god distributes in his anger?
Job 21:18:
they are like straw before the wind,
    and like chaff that a storm carries away.
Job 21:19:
god stores up their iniquity for their children;
    let him reward the people themselves, and they will know it.
Job 21:20:
let their eyes see their own destruction,
    and let them drink of the wrath of the almighty.
Job 21:21:
for what do they care about their households after them,
    when the number of their months is cut off?
Job 21:22:
“can anyone teach god knowledge,
    since he judges those who are on high?
Job 21:23:
one dies in his full strength,
    being wholly at ease and secure.
Job 21:24:
his pails are full of milk,
    and the marrow of his bones is moist.
Job 21:25:
another dies in the bitterness of his soul,
    never having eaten with pleasure.
Job 21:26:
they will lie down alike in the dust,
    and worms will cover them.
Job 21:27:
“behold, i know your thoughts,
    and the schemes with which you would wrong me.
Job 21:28:
for you say, ‘where is the house of the prince?
    and where are the dwelling places of the wicked?’
Job 21:29:
have you not asked them who travel the road?
    and do you not know their signs?
Job 21:30:
for the wicked are reserved for the day of destruction;
    they will be brought forth on the day of wrath.
Job 21:31:
who will declare his way to his face?
    and who will repay him for what he has done?
Job 21:32:
yet will he be brought to the grave
    and will remain in the tomb.
Job 21:34:
“how then can you comfort me with emptiness,
    since deceit remains in your answers?”
Job 22:2:
“can a man be profitable to god,
    as he who is wise may be profitable to himself?
Job 22:3:
is it any pleasure to the almighty that you are righteous?
    or is it gain to him that you make your ways blameless?
Job 22:4:
“is it because of your fear of him that he corrects you,
    and enters into judgment with you?
Job 22:5:
is not your wickedness great,
    and your iniquity infinite?
Job 22:6:
for you have taken a pledge from your brother for nothing,
    and stripped the naked of their clothing.
Job 22:7:
you have not given water to the weary to drink,
    and you have withheld bread from the hungry.
Job 22:8:
but as for the mighty man, he possessed the earth,
    and the honorable man lived in it.
Job 22:9:
you have sent widows away empty,
    and the strength of the fatherless was crushed.
Job 22:10:
therefore snares are all around you,
    and sudden fear troubles you,
Job 22:11:
or darkness, so that you cannot see;
    and an abundance of waters covers you.
Job 22:12:
“is not god in the height of heaven?
    and see the height of the stars, how high they are!
Job 22:13:
and you say, ‘what does god know?
    can he judge through the dark cloud?
Job 22:14:
thick clouds are his covering, so he cannot see;
    and he walks above the circle of heaven.’
Job 22:15:
will you keep to the old way,
    that wicked men have trod?
Job 22:16:
they were cut down before their time;
    their foundations were swept away by a flood.
Job 22:17:
they said to god, ‘depart from us,’
    and, ‘what can the almighty do to us?’
Job 22:18:
yet he filled their houses with good things;
    but the counsel of the wicked is far from me.
Job 22:19:
“the righteous see it and are glad,
    and the innocent laugh them to scorn:
Job 22:20:
‘surely our adversaries are cut down,
    and the fire consumes their remnant.’
Job 22:21:
“now acquaint yourself with him and be at peace;
    thereby good will come to you.
Job 22:22:
receive, i pray, the teaching from his mouth,
    and lay up his words in your heart.
Job 22:23:
if you return to the almighty, you will be built up;
    you will put away iniquity far from your tents.
Job 22:24:
then you will lay up gold as dust,
    and the gold of ophir as the stones of the brooks.
Job 22:25:
yes, the almighty will be your gold
    and your precious silver;
Job 22:26:
for then you will delight yourself in the almighty,
    and will lift up your face unto god.
Job 22:27:
you will make your prayer to him, and he will hear you,
    and you will pay your vows.
Job 22:28:
you will also declare a matter, and it will be established unto you;
    and the light will shine upon your ways.
Job 22:29:
when men are cast down, and you say, ‘there is a time of exaltation!’
    then he will save the humble person.
Job 22:30:
he will even deliver one who is not innocent;
    he will be delivered by the purity of your hands.”
Job 23:2:
“today also my complaint is bitter;
    my hand is heavy because of my groaning.
Job 23:3:
oh, that i knew where i might find him,
    that i might come even to his seat!
Job 23:4:
i would present my case before him
    and fill my mouth with arguments.
Job 23:5:
i would know the words that he would answer me
    and understand what he would say to me.
Job 23:6:
will he plead against me with his great power?
    no! but he would take note of me.
Job 23:7:
there the righteous might dispute with him;
    so would i be delivered forever from my judge.
Job 23:8:
“look, i go forward, but he is not there,
    and backward, but i cannot perceive him;
Job 23:9:
when he works on the left hand, i cannot behold him;
    he turns to the right hand, i cannot see him.
Job 23:10:
but he knows the way that i take;
    when he has tested me, i will come forth as gold.
Job 23:11:
my foot has held fast to his steps;
    i have kept his way and have not turned aside.
Job 23:12:
i have not departed from the commandment of his lips;
    i have esteemed the words of his mouth more than my necessary food.
Job 23:13:
“but he is resolute, and who can turn him?
    and whatever his soul desires, that he does.
Job 23:14:
for he performs what is appointed for me,
    and many such things are with him.
Job 23:15:
therefore i am troubled at his presence;
    when i consider, i am afraid of him.
Job 23:16:
for god makes my heart soft,
    and the almighty troubles me;
Job 23:17:
because i was not cut off from the presence of darkness,
    nor has he covered the darkness from my face.
Job 24:1:
“since times of judgment are not kept by the almighty,
    why do they who know him not see his days?
Job 24:2:
some remove the landmarks;
    they violently take away flocks and feed on them.
Job 24:3:
they drive away the donkey of the orphan;
    they take the widow’s ox for a pledge.
Job 24:4:
they turn away the needy;
    the poor of the earth are forced to hide.
Job 24:5:
behold, as wild donkeys in the desert,
    they go out to their work, rising early for a prey.
    the wilderness yields food for them and for their children.
Job 24:6:
they gather their fodder in the field,
    and they glean in the vineyard of the wicked.
Job 24:7:
they cause the naked to lodge without clothing,
    and they have no covering in the cold.
Job 24:8:
they are wet with the showers of the mountains
    and embrace the rock for want of a shelter.
Job 24:9:
they snatch the fatherless from the breast
    and take a pledge from the poor.
Job 24:10:
they cause him to go naked without clothing,
    and they take away the sheaf from the hungry.
Job 24:11:
they press out oil within their walls
    and tread their winepresses, yet suffer thirst.
Job 24:14:
the murderer, rising with the light, kills the poor and needy,
    and in the night he is like a thief.
Job 24:18:
“he is swift as the waters.
    their portion is cursed in the earth.
    they do not turn toward the way of the vineyards.
Job 24:19:
drought and heat consume the snow waters;
    so the grave consumes those who have sinned.
Job 24:21:
he preys on the barren who do not bear,
    and does no good for the widow.
Job 24:22:
but god draws the mighty away with his power;
    he rises up, and no man is sure of life.
Job 24:23:
he gives them security, and they rely on it;
    yet his eyes are on their ways.
Job 24:25:
“if it is not so, who will prove me a liar
    and make my speech worth nothing?”
Job 25:2:
“dominion and fear are with him;
    he makes peace in his high places.
Job 25:3:
is there any number to his armies?
    and upon whom does his light not rise?
Job 25:4:
how then can man be righteous with god?
    or how can he who is born of a woman be clean?
Job 25:5:
behold, even the moon does not shine,
    and the stars are not pure in his sight;
Job 25:6:
how much less man, who is a maggot?
    and the son of man, who is a worm?”
Job 26:2:
“how have you helped him who is without power?
    how have you saved the arm that has no strength?
Job 26:3:
how have you counseled him who has no wisdom?
    and how have you plentifully declared sound knowledge?
Job 26:4:
to whom have you uttered words?
    and whose breath came from you?
Job 26:5:
“the departed spirits tremble under the waters,
    and their inhabitants.
Job 26:6:
the underworld is naked before him,
    and destruction has no covering.
Job 26:7:
he stretches out the north over empty space,
    he hangs the earth upon nothing.
Job 26:8:
he binds up the waters in his thick clouds,
    and the cloud is not broken under them.
Job 26:9:
he covers the face of the full moon
    and spreads his cloud over it.
Job 26:10:
he has circled the waters with boundaries,
    until the day and night come to an end.
Job 26:11:
the pillars of heaven tremble
    and are astonished at his reproof.
Job 26:12:
he divides the sea with his power,
    and by his understanding he strikes through the proud.
Job 26:13:
by his breath he has made fair the heavens;
    his hand has formed the fleeing serpent.
Job 26:14:
indeed, these are but a part of his ways,
    and how small a whisper we hear of him!
    but the thunder of his power who can understand?”
Job 27:2:
“as god lives, who has taken away my judgment,
    and the almighty, who has made my soul bitter,
Job 27:3:
all the while my spirit is in me,
    and the breath of god is in my nostrils,
Job 27:4:
my lips will not speak wickedness,
    nor my tongue utter deceit.
Job 27:5:
god forbid that i should justify you.
    until i die i will not put away my integrity from me.
Job 27:6:
my righteousness i hold fast and will not let it go;
    my heart will not reproach me as long as i live.
Job 27:7:
“let my enemy be like the wicked,
    and he who rises up against me like the unrighteous.
Job 27:8:
for what is the hope of the hypocrite,
    though he may gain much, when god takes away his soul?
Job 27:9:
will god hear his cry
    when trouble comes upon him?
Job 27:10:
will he delight himself in the almighty?
    will he always call upon god?
Job 27:11:
“i will teach you about the hand of god;
    what is with the almighty i will not conceal.
Job 27:12:
look, all of you have seen it;
    why then have you become altogether vain?
Job 27:13:
“this is the portion of a wicked man with god,
    and the inheritance that oppressors receive from the almighty:
Job 27:14:
if his children are multiplied, it is for the sword,
    and his offspring will not be satisfied with bread.
Job 27:15:
those who survive him will be buried in death,
    and their widows will not weep.
Job 27:16:
though he heaps up silver like the dust
    and piles up clothing like the clay—
Job 27:17:
he may pile it up, but the just will wear it,
    and the innocent will divide the silver.
Job 27:18:
he builds his house like a moth,
    and like a booth that the watchman makes.
Job 27:19:
the rich man will lie down, but he will not be gathered;
    he opens his eyes, and he is not.
Job 27:20:
terrors overtake him like floodwaters;
    a tempest steals him away in the night.
Job 27:21:
the east wind carries him away, and he departs;
    it sweeps him out of his place.
Job 27:22:
for god will cast it upon him and not spare;
    he would flee from its power.
Job 27:23:
men will clap their hands at him
    and will hiss him out of his place.
Job 28:1:
“surely there is a mine for the silver,
    and a place where they refine gold.
Job 28:2:
iron is taken out of the earth,
    and copper is smelted from the ore.
Job 28:3:
man puts an end to darkness,
    and searches every extremity
    for ore in the darkness and the shadow of death.
Job 28:5:
as for the earth, from it comes bread,
    and underneath it is turned up as by fire.
Job 28:6:
its stones are the source of sapphires,
    and it has dust of gold.
Job 28:7:
there is a path that no bird knows,
    and that the vulture’s eye has not seen;
Job 28:8:
the lion cubs have not trodden it,
    nor has the fierce lion passed by it.
Job 28:9:
he puts forth his hand upon the rock;
    he overturns the mountains by the roots.
Job 28:10:
he cuts out rivers among the rocks,
    and his eye sees every precious thing.
Job 28:11:
he prevents the floods from overflowing,
    and the thing that is hidden he brings forth to light.
Job 28:12:
“but where will wisdom be found?
    and where is the place of understanding?
Job 28:13:
man does not know its price,
    nor is it found in the land of the living.
Job 28:14:
the depth says, ‘it is not in me,’
    and the sea says, ‘it is not with me.’
Job 28:15:
it cannot be bought for gold,
    nor can silver be weighed for its price.
Job 28:16:
it cannot be valued in the gold of ophir,
    with the precious onyx or the sapphire.
Job 28:17:
the gold and the crystal cannot equal it,
    and it cannot be exchanged for jewels of fine gold.
Job 28:18:
no mention will be made of coral or of pearls,
    for the price of wisdom is above rubies.
Job 28:19:
the topaz of ethiopia will not equal it,
    nor will it be valued with pure gold.
Job 28:20:
“from where then does wisdom come?
    and where is the place of understanding?
Job 28:21:
it is hidden from the eyes of all living
    and concealed from the birds of the air.
Job 28:22:
destruction and death say,
    ‘we have heard of its fame with our ears.’
Job 28:23:
god understands its way,
    and he knows its place.
Job 28:24:
for he looks to the ends of the earth,
    and sees under the whole heaven,
Job 28:25:
to make the weight of the wind,
    and he weighs the waters by measure.
Job 28:26:
when he made a decree for the rain,
    and a path for the lightning of the thunder,
Job 28:27:
then he saw it and declared it;
    he prepared it, yes, and searched it out.
Job 29:2:
“oh, that i were as in months past,
    as in the days when god watched over me;
Job 29:3:
when his lamp shone upon my head,
    and when by his light i walked through darkness;
Job 29:4:
as i was in the days of my autumn youth,
    when the friendly counsel of god was over my tent;
Job 29:5:
when the almighty was still with me,
    when my children were around me;
Job 29:6:
when my steps were bathed in butter,
    and the rock poured out rivers of oil for me!
Job 29:7:
“when i went out to the gate of the city,
    when i took my seat in the square,
Job 29:8:
the young men saw me and hid themselves,
    and the aged arose and stood up.
Job 29:9:
the princes refrained from talking,
    and put their hand on their mouth.
Job 29:10:
the nobles held their peace,
    and their tongue stuck to the roof of their mouth.
Job 29:11:
when the ear heard, then it blessed me;
    and when the eye saw, then it approved me,
Job 29:12:
because i delivered the poor who cried,
    and the fatherless, and him who had none to help him.
Job 29:13:
the blessing of the perishing man came upon me,
    and i caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy.
Job 29:14:
i put on righteousness, and it clothed me;
    my judgment was like a robe and a diadem.
Job 29:15:
i was eyes for the blind,
    and i was feet for the lame.
Job 29:16:
i was a father to the poor,
    and i searched out the case that i did not know.
Job 29:17:
i broke the jaws of the wicked
    and plucked the victim from his teeth.
Job 29:18:
“then i said, ‘i will die in my nest,
    and i will multiply my days as the sand.
Job 29:19:
my root was spread out by the waters,
    and the dew lay all night upon my branch.
Job 29:20:
my glory was fresh in me,
    and my bow was renewed in my hand.’
Job 29:21:
“men listened to me and waited,
    and kept silence for my counsel.
Job 29:22:
after my words they did not speak again,
    and my speech settled on them like dew.
Job 29:23:
they waited for me as for the rain,
    and they opened their mouth wide as for the spring rain.
Job 29:24:
if i mocked at them, they did not believe it,
    and the light of my countenance they did not cast down.
Job 29:25:
i chose the way for them and sat as chief,
    and lived as a king in the army,
    as one who comforts mourners.
Job 30:1:
“but now those who are younger than i mock me,
    whose fathers i disdained to put with the dogs of my flock.
Job 30:2:
yes, how does the strength of their hands profit me?
    their vigor has perished.
Job 30:4:
who pluck mallow by the bushes,
    and juniper roots for their food.
Job 30:5:
they were driven out from among men;
    they shout after them as after a thief.
Job 30:6:
they had to dwell in the rocky riverbeds,
    in caves of the earth, and in the rocks.
Job 30:7:
among the bushes they brayed;
    under the nettles they were gathered together.
Job 30:8:
they were children of fools, yes, children of vile men;
    they were scourged from the earth.
Job 30:9:
“now i am their taunting song;
    yes, i am their byword.
Job 30:10:
they abhor me, they flee far from me;
    they do not hesitate to spit in my face.
Job 30:11:
because he has loosed my bowstring and afflicted me,
    they have cast off the bridle before me.
Job 30:14:
they came upon me as a wide breach, with a crash they came;
    in the desolation they rolled themselves upon me.
Job 30:16:
“now my soul is poured out within me;
    the days of affliction have taken hold of me.
Job 30:17:
my bones are pierced in me at night,
    and my sinews have no rest.
Job 30:18:
by the great force of my disease my garment is changed;
    it binds me about as the collar of my coat.
Job 30:19:
he has cast me into the mire,
    and i have become like dust and ashes.
Job 30:20:
“i cry unto you, but you do not hear me;
    i stand up, and you do not regard me.
Job 30:21:
you have become cruel to me;
    with your strong hand you oppose me.
Job 30:22:
you lift me up to the wind and cause me to ride on it;
    you dissolve my success.
Job 30:23:
for i know that you will bring me to death,
    and to the house appointed for all living.
Job 30:24:
“surely he will not stretch out his hand to the grave,
    though they cry when he destroys it.
Job 30:25:
did i not weep for him who was in trouble?
    was not my soul grieved for the poor?
Job 30:26:
when i looked for good, then evil disaster came upon me;
    and when i waited for light, darkness came.
Job 30:27:
my insides boiled and did not rest;
    the days of affliction have met me.
Job 30:28:
i went mourning without the sun;
    i stood up, and i cried in the congregation.
Job 30:29:
i am a brother of jackals
    and a companion of owls.
Job 30:30:
my skin is black upon me,
    and my bones are burned with fever.
Job 30:31:
my harp is turned to mourning,
    and my flute to the voice of those who weep.
Job 31:1:
“i made a covenant with my eyes;
    why then should i look upon a young woman?
Job 31:2:
for what portion of god is there from above?
    and what inheritance of the almighty from on high?
Job 31:3:
does not destruction belong to the wicked,
    and calamity to the workers of iniquity?
Job 31:4:
does he not see my ways,
    and count all my steps?
Job 31:5:
“if i have walked in vanity,
    or if my foot has hurried after deceit,
Job 31:6:
let me be weighed in an even balance
    that god may know my integrity.
Job 31:8:
then let me sow, but let another eat;
    yes, let my offspring be rooted out.
Job 31:9:
“if my heart has been deceived by a woman,
    or if i have laid wait at my neighbor’s door,
Job 31:10:
then let my wife grind for another,
    and let others bow down over her.
Job 31:11:
for this is a heinous crime;
    yes, it is an iniquity to be punished by the judges.
Job 31:12:
for it is a fire that consumes to destruction
    and would root out all my increase.
Job 31:13:
“if i have despised the cause of my male or female servant
    when they complained against me,
Job 31:14:
what then will i do when god rises up?
    and when he visits, what will i answer him?
Job 31:15:
did not he who made me in the womb make him?
    and did not the same one fashion us in the womb?
Job 31:16:
“if i have kept the poor from their desire,
    or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail,
Job 31:17:
or have eaten my morsel by myself,
    so that the fatherless could not eat of it
Job 31:18:
(but from my youth he was brought up with me, as with a father,
    and i have guided the widow from my mother’s womb);
Job 31:19:
if i have seen anyone perish for lack of clothing,
    or any poor without covering;
Job 31:20:
if his body has not blessed me,
    and if he was not warmed with the fleece of my sheep;
Job 31:21:
if i have lifted up my hand against the fatherless,
    when i saw i had help in the gate;
Job 31:22:
then let my arm fall from my shoulder blade,
    and my arm be broken from the bone.
Job 31:23:
for destruction from god is a terror to me,
    and because of his highness i cannot endure.
Job 31:24:
“if i have made gold my hope,
    or have said to the fine gold, ‘you are my confidence’;
Job 31:25:
if i rejoiced because my wealth was great,
    and because my hand had gained much;
Job 31:26:
if i saw the sun when it shined,
    or the moon moving in brightness;
Job 31:27:
and my heart has been secretly enticed,
    or my mouth has kissed my hand;
Job 31:28:
this also would be an iniquity to be punished by the judge,
    for i would have denied the god who is above.
Job 31:29:
“if i rejoiced at the destruction of him who hated me,
    or lifted up myself when disaster found him
Job 31:30:
(nor have i allowed my mouth to sin
    by wishing for a curse on his soul);
Job 31:31:
if the men of my tent have not said,
    ‘who is there who has not been satisfied with his meat?’
Job 31:32:
(the stranger has not lodged in the street,
    but i opened my doors to the traveler);
Job 31:33:
if i covered my transgressions as any man,
    by hiding my iniquity in my heart,
Job 31:34:
did i fear a great multitude,
    or did the contempt of families terrify me,
    so that i kept silence, and did not go out of the door?
Job 31:35:
“oh, that one would hear me!
    behold, my desire is that the almighty would answer me,
    and that the one who contends against me had written a book!
Job 31:36:
surely i would carry it on my shoulder
    and bind it on me like a crown.
Job 31:37:
i would declare to him the number of my steps;
    like a prince i would approach him.
Job 31:38:
“if my land cries out against me,
    and its furrows also weep together;
Job 31:39:
if i have eaten its fruit without money,
    or have caused its owners to lose their life;
Job 32:1: so these three men ceased answering job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.

Job 32:3: his wrath was aroused also against his three friends because they had found no answer and yet had condemned job.
Job 32:4: now elihu had waited until job had spoken because they were older than he.
Job 32:5: when elihu saw that there was no answer in the mouth of these three men, then his wrath was aroused.
Job 32:6:
elihu the son of barakel the buzite answered:
“i am young,
    and you are very old;
therefore i was afraid
    and dared not show you my opinion.
Job 32:7:
i said, ‘age should speak,
    and multitude of years should teach wisdom.’
Job 32:8:
but there is a spirit in man,
    and the breath of the almighty gives him understanding.
Job 32:9:
great men are not always wise,
    nor do the aged always understand judgment.
Job 32:10:
“therefore i say,
    ‘listen to me; i will also declare my opinion.’
Job 32:13:
lest you say, ‘we have found wisdom’;
    god will subdue him, not man.
Job 32:14:
now he has not directed his words against me,
    so i will not answer him with your speeches.
Job 32:15:
“they are amazed; they answer no more;
    they cease speaking.
Job 32:16:
and i have waited,
    (for they did not speak, but stood still and answered no more).
Job 32:17:
i said, ‘i also will answer my part;
    i too will show my opinion.’
Job 32:18:
for i am full of words;
    the spirit within me compels me.
Job 32:19:
see, my belly is like wine that has no vent;
    it is ready to burst like new wineskins.
Job 32:20:
i will speak, that i may be refreshed;
    i will open my lips and answer.
Job 32:21:
let me not, i pray, show partiality to anyone,
    nor let me give flattering titles to man.
Job 32:22:
for i do not know how to give flattering titles;
    in so doing my maker would soon take me away.
Job 33:1:
“therefore, job, i pray, hear my speeches,
    and listen to all my words.
Job 33:2:
behold, now i have opened my mouth;
    my tongue has spoken in my mouth.
Job 33:3:
my words will be from the uprightness of my heart,
    and my lips will utter knowledge clearly.
Job 33:4:
the spirit of god has made me,
    and the breath of the almighty has given me life.
Job 33:5:
if you can answer me,
    set your words in order before me; stand up.
Job 33:6:
surely i am before god like you;
    i also am formed out of the clay.
Job 33:7:
indeed, no dread of me will make you afraid,
    nor will my hand be heavy upon you.
Job 33:8:
“surely you have spoken in my hearing,
    and i have heard the sound of your words, saying,
Job 33:9:
‘i am clean, without transgression;
    i am innocent, nor is there iniquity in me.
Job 33:10:
behold, he finds occasions against me,
    he counts me for his enemy;
Job 33:11:
he puts my feet in the stocks,
    he watches all my paths.’
Job 33:12:
“look, in this you are not just.
    i will answer you, that god is greater than man.
Job 33:13:
why do you strive against him?
    for he does not give an accounting for any of his words.
Job 33:14:
for god speaks once, yes twice,
    yet man does not perceive it.
Job 33:15:
in a dream, in a vision of the night,
    when deep sleep falls upon men,
    in slumber on their beds,
Job 33:16:
then he opens the ears of men,
    and seals their instruction,
Job 33:17:
that he might turn aside man from his purpose,
    and conceal pride from man.
Job 33:18:
he keeps back his soul from the pit,
    and his life from perishing by the sword.
Job 33:19:
“he is also chastened with pain on his bed,
    and with strong pain in many of his bones,
Job 33:20:
so that his life abhors bread,
    and his soul dainty food.
Job 33:21:
his flesh is consumed away that it cannot be seen,
    and his bones that were not seen stick out.
Job 33:22:
yes, his soul draws near to the grave,
    and his life to the executioners.
Job 33:25:
his flesh will be fresher than a child’s;
    he will return to the days of his youth;
Job 33:26:
he will pray to god, and he will be favorable unto him,
    and he will see his face with joy,
    for he will render unto man his righteousness.
Job 33:27:
then he looks at men and says,
    ‘i have sinned and perverted what was right,
    and it did not profit me.’
Job 33:28:
he will deliver his soul from going down to the pit,
    and his life will see the light.
Job 33:29:
“behold, god works all these things,
    twice, three times with man,
Job 33:30:
to bring back his soul from the pit,
    to be enlightened with the light of the living.
Job 33:31:
“pay attention, job, listen to me;
    hold your peace, and i will speak.
Job 33:32:
if you have anything to say, answer me;
    speak, for i desire to justify you.
Job 33:33:
if not, listen to me; hold your peace,
    and i will teach you wisdom.”
Job 34:2:
“hear my words, o you wise men;
    and give ear unto me, you that have knowledge.
Job 34:3:
for the ear tests words,
    as the mouth tastes food.
Job 34:4:
let us choose justice for ourselves;
    let us know among ourselves what is good.
Job 34:5:
“for job has said, ‘i am righteous,
    but god has taken away my judgment.
Job 34:6:
should i lie concerning my right?
    my wound is incurable, though i am without transgression.’
Job 34:7:
what man is like job,
    who drinks scorn like water,
Job 34:8:
who goes in company with the workers of iniquity
    and walks with wicked men?
Job 34:9:
for he has said, ‘it profits a man nothing
    that he should delight himself in god.’
Job 34:10:

good and upright is the lord;

Psalm 25:9:

Psalm 25:10:
all the paths of the lord are lovingkindness and truth,

Psalm 25:11:

Psalm 25:12:
who is the man who fears the lord?

Psalm 25:13:
he will dwell at ease,

Psalm 25:14:
the counsel of the lord is with those who fear him,

Psalm 25:15:
my eyes are ever toward the lord,

Psalm 25:16:
turn to me, and be gracious to me,

Psalm 25:17:
the troubles of my heart are enlarged;

Psalm 25:18:
look on my pain and misery,

Psalm 25:19:
consider my enemies, for they are many,

Psalm 25:21:
truth and integrity will preserve me

Psalm 25:22:

Psalm 26:1:
judge me, o lord,
    for i have walked in my integrity.
i have trusted in the lord;
    i will not slip.
Psalm 26:2:
examine me, o lord, and test me;
    try my affections and my heart.
Psalm 26:3:
for your lovingkindness is before my eyes,
    and i have walked in your truth.
Psalm 26:4:
i have not sat with the worthless,
    nor will i go with hypocrites.
Psalm 26:5:
i have hated the congregation of evildoers,
    and will not sit with the wicked.
Psalm 26:6:
i will wash my hands in innocence;

Psalm 26:7:
that i may proclaim with the voice of thanksgiving,
    and tell of all your wondrous works.
Psalm 26:8:
lord, i have loved the refuge of your house,

Psalm 26:9:
do not gather my soul with sinners,

Psalm 26:10:
in whose hands is wickedness,
    and their right hand is full of bribes.
Psalm 26:11:
but as for me, i will walk in my integrity;

Psalm 26:12:
my foot stands in an even place;

Psalm 27:3:
though an army should encamp against me,

though war should rise against me,

Psalm 27:4:
one thing i have asked from the lord,

for me to dwell in the house of the lord

to see the beauty of the lord,

Psalm 27:7:
hear, o lord, when i cry with my voice!

Psalm 27:8:
when you said, “seek my face,”

Psalm 27:10:
if my father and my mother forsake me,

Psalm 27:11:

i believe

let your lovingkindness, o lord, be on us,

evil will slay the wicked,

the lord redeems the life of his servants,

they rewarded me evil for good,

Psalm 35:16:
with hypocritical mockers in feasts,

Psalm 35:17:
lord, how long will you look on?
    rescue my soul from their destructions,

may my deceitful enemies

they opened their mouth wide against me,

rouse yourself and awake for my judgment,

may those who favor my righteous cause

they also do no wrong;
    they walk in his ways.
Psalm 119:4:
you have commanded us
    to keep your precepts diligently.
Psalm 119:5:
oh, that my ways were established
    to keep your statutes!
Psalm 119:6:
then i shall not be ashamed,
    when i have my focus on all your commandments.
Psalm 119:7:
i will praise you with an upright heart,
    when i have learned your righteous judgments.
Psalm 119:8:
i will keep your statutes;
    do not completely abandon me.
Psalm 119:9:
how shall a young man keep his way pure?
    by keeping it according to your word.
Psalm 119:10:
with my whole heart i seek you;
    do not allow me to wander from your commandments.
Psalm 119:11:
your word i have hidden in my heart,
    that i might not sin against you.
Psalm 119:12:
blessed are you, o lord;
    teach me your statutes.
Psalm 119:13:
with my lips i declare
    all the decrees of your mouth.
Psalm 119:14:
i rejoice in the way of your testimonies,
    as much as in all riches.
Psalm 119:15:
i will meditate on your precepts
    and keep my eyes on your ways.
Psalm 119:16:
i will delight in your statutes;
    i will not forget your word.
Psalm 119:17:
deal kindly with your servant, that i may live
    and keep your word.
Psalm 119:18:
open my eyes, that i may behold
    wondrous things from your law.
Psalm 119:19:
i am a sojourner in the land;
    do not hide your commandments from me.
Psalm 119:20:
my soul is consumed all the time
    with a longing for your decrees.
Psalm 119:21:
you have rebuked the proud, those cursed,
    who depart from your commandments.
Psalm 119:22:
remove from me reproach and contempt,
    for i have kept your testimonies.
Psalm 119:23:
even if princes sit and conspire against me,
    your servant will meditate on your statutes.
Psalm 119:24:
your testimonies are my delight
    and my counselors.
Psalm 119:25:
my soul clings to the dust;
    revive me according to your word.
Psalm 119:26:
i have declared my ways, and you heard me;
    teach me your statutes.
Psalm 119:27:
make me to understand the way of your precepts;
    then i shall contemplate on your wondrous works.
Psalm 119:28:
my soul collapses on account of grief;
    strengthen me according to your word.
Psalm 119:29:
remove from me the way of falsehood,
    and graciously grant me your law.
Psalm 119:30:
i have chosen the way of faithfulness;
    your judgments i have laid before me.
Psalm 119:31:
i have stayed with your testimonies, o lord;
    may i not be put to shame.
Psalm 119:32:
i will run in the way of your commandments,
    when you set my heart free.
Psalm 119:33:
teach me, o lord, the way of your statutes,
    and i shall keep it to the end.
Psalm 119:34:
give me understanding, and i shall keep your law
    and observe it with my whole heart.
Psalm 119:35:
lead me in the path of your commandments,
    for i delight in them.
Psalm 119:36:
incline my heart unto your testimonies,
    and not for unjust gain.
Psalm 119:37:
turn away my eyes from beholding worthlessness,
    and revive me in your way.
Psalm 119:38:
establish your word to your servant,
    so that you are feared.
Psalm 119:39:
turn away my reproach that i dread,
    for your judgments are good.
Psalm 119:40:
behold, i have a longing for your precepts;
    revive me in your righteousness.
Psalm 119:41:
let your mercies come to me, o lord,
    even your deliverance according to your word.
Psalm 119:42:
so i shall have an answer for him who reproaches me,
    for i trust in your word.
Psalm 119:43:
do not take the word of truth out of my mouth,
    for i have hoped in your judgments.
Psalm 119:44:
so i shall keep your law continually,
    forever and ever.
Psalm 119:45:
i will walk in an open space,
    for i seek your precepts.
Psalm 119:46:
i will speak of your testimonies also before kings
    and will not be ashamed.
Psalm 119:47:
i will delight in your commandments,
    which i have loved.
Psalm 119:48:
my hands i will lift up unto your commandments, which i have loved;
    i will meditate on your statutes.
Psalm 119:49:
remember your word to your servant,
    on which you have caused me to hope.
Psalm 119:50:
this is my comfort in my affliction,
    for your word revives me.
Psalm 119:51:
the proud ones have derided me,
    yet i have not forsaken your law.
Psalm 119:52:
i remembered your judgments of old, o lord,
    and i have comforted myself.
Psalm 119:53:
fury has taken hold of me because of the wicked
    who forsake your law.
Psalm 119:54:
your statutes have been my songs
    in the house of my temporary dwelling.
Psalm 119:55:
i have remembered your name, o lord, in the night,
    and have kept your law.
Psalm 119:56:
this is my blessing,
    because i have kept your precepts.
Psalm 119:57:
you are my portion, o lord;
    i have said that i would keep your words.
Psalm 119:58:
i seek your favor with my whole heart;
    be merciful to me according to your word.
Psalm 119:59:
i consider my ways,
    and i turn my feet to your testimonies.
Psalm 119:60:
i made haste, and i did not delay
    to keep your commandments.
Psalm 119:61:
the bands of the wicked have trapped me,
    but i have not forgotten your law.
Psalm 119:62:
at midnight i will rise to give thanks to you,
    because of your righteous judgments.
Psalm 119:63:
i am a companion of all who fear you,
    and of those who keep your precepts.
Psalm 119:64:
the earth, o lord, is full of your mercy;
    teach me your statutes.
Psalm 119:65:
you have been good to your servant,
    o lord, according to your word.
Psalm 119:66:
teach me good discernment and knowledge,
    for i have believed your commandments.
Psalm 119:67:
before i was afflicted i wandered,
    but now i keep your word.
Psalm 119:68:
you are good and do good;
    teach me your statutes.
Psalm 119:69:
the proud have spoken lies against me,
    but i keep your precepts with my whole heart.
Psalm 119:70:
their heart is as thick as fat,
    but i delight in your law.
Psalm 119:71:
it is good for me that i have been afflicted,
    that i might learn your statutes.
Psalm 119:72:
the law from your mouth is better to me
    than thousands of gold and silver coins.
Psalm 119:73:
your hands have made me and fashioned me;
    give me understanding, that i may learn your commandments.
Psalm 119:74:
those who fear you will be glad when they see me,
    because i have hoped in your word.
Psalm 119:75:
i know, o lord, that your judgments are right,
    and that you in faithfulness have afflicted me.
Psalm 119:76:
let your merciful kindness comfort me,
    according to your word to your servant.
Psalm 119:77:
let your compassion come to me, that i may live,
    for your law is my delight.
Psalm 119:78:
let the proud be ashamed, for they have been wicked to me in falsehood,
    but i will meditate on your precepts.
Psalm 119:79:
let those who fear you turn to me,
    that they might know your testimonies.
Psalm 119:80:
let my heart be blameless in your statutes,
    that i may not be ashamed.
Psalm 119:81:
my soul longs for your deliverance,
    but i hope in your word.
Psalm 119:82:
my eyes are weary for your word,
    saying, “when will you comfort me?”
Psalm 119:83:
for i have become like a wineskin dried in the smoke,
    yet i have not forgotten your statutes.
Psalm 119:84:
how many days are given to your servant?
    when will you provide judgment on those who persecute me?
Psalm 119:85:
the proud have dug pits for me,
    and they do not live in accordance to your law.
Psalm 119:86:
all your commandments are faithful;
    i am persecuted without cause; help me!
Psalm 119:87:
they have almost consumed me on the earth,
    but i have not abandoned your precepts.
Psalm 119:88:
revive me according to your lovingkindness,
    that i may keep the testimony from your mouth.
Psalm 119:89:
forever, o lord, your word
    is established in heaven.
Psalm 119:90:
your faithfulness is for all generations;
    you have established the earth, and it is firm.
Psalm 119:91:
they continue this day according to your ordinance,
    for all are your servants.
Psalm 119:92:
unless your law had been my delight,
    i would have perished in my affliction.
Psalm 119:93:
i will never forget your precepts,
    for with them you have revived me.
Psalm 119:94:
i am yours; deliver me,
    for i have sought your precepts.
Psalm 119:95:
the wicked have waited to destroy me,
    but i will consider your testimonies.
Psalm 119:96:
i have seen that all perfection has an end,
    but your commandment is quite broad.
Psalm 119:97:
oh, how i love your law!
    it is my meditation all the day.
Psalm 119:98:
your commandments have made me wiser than my enemies,
    for they are continually with me.
Psalm 119:99:
i have more understanding than all my teachers,
    for your testimonies are my meditation.
Psalm 119:100:
i understand more than the elders,
    because i keep your precepts.
Psalm 119:101:
i have restrained my feet from every evil way,
    that i might keep your word.
Psalm 119:102:
i have not departed from your judgments,
    for you have taught me.
Psalm 119:103:
how sweet are your words to the taste of my mouth!
    sweeter than honey to my mouth!
Psalm 119:104:
through your precepts i receive understanding;
    therefore i hate every false way.
Psalm 119:105:
your word is a lamp to my feet
    and a light to my path.
Psalm 119:106:
i have sworn, and i will perform it,
    that i will keep your righteous judgments.
Psalm 119:107:
i am greatly afflicted;
    revive me, o lord, according to your word.
Psalm 119:108:
accept the freewill offerings of my praise, o lord,
    and teach me your judgments.
Psalm 119:109:
my soul is continually in my hand,
    yet i do not forget your law.
Psalm 119:110:
the wicked have laid a trap for me,
    yet i do not depart from your precepts.
Psalm 119:111:
your testimonies are my inheritance forever,
    for they are the rejoicing of my heart.
Psalm 119:112:
i have inclined my heart to perform your statutes always,
    even unto the end.
Psalm 119:113:
i hate those who are double-minded,
    but i love your law.
Psalm 119:114:
you are my hiding place and my shield,
    i hope in your word.
Psalm 119:115:
depart from me, you who are wicked,
    for i keep the commandments of my god.
Psalm 119:116:
uphold me according to your word, that i may live,
    and let me not be ashamed with my hope.
Psalm 119:117:
hold me up, and i shall be safe,
    and i will have respect for your statutes continually.
Psalm 119:118:
you have rejected all those who stray from your statutes,
    for their deceit is falsehood.
Psalm 119:119:
you put away all the wicked of the earth like dross;
    therefore i love your testimonies.
Psalm 119:120:
my body trembles for fear of you,
    and i am afraid of your judgments.
Psalm 119:121:
i have done what is right and just;
    do not abandon me to my oppressors.
Psalm 119:122:
be true to your servant for good;
    let not the proud ones oppress me.
Psalm 119:123:
my eyes long for your deliverance
    and for the promise of your righteousness.
Psalm 119:124:
deal with your servant according to your mercy,
    and teach me your statutes.
Psalm 119:125:
i am your servant; grant me understanding,
    that i may know your testimonies.
Psalm 119:126:
it is time for you, o lord, to act,
    for they have broken your law.
Psalm 119:127:
therefore i love your commandments
    above gold, even fine gold.
Psalm 119:128:
for i follow all your precepts to be right,
    and i hate every false way.
Psalm 119:129:
your testimonies are wonderful;
    therefore my soul keeps them.
Psalm 119:130:
the giving of your words gives light;
    it grants understanding to the simple.
Psalm 119:131:
i opened my mouth and panted,
    for i long for your commandments.
Psalm 119:132:
look upon me, and be merciful to me,
    as you are for those who love your name.
Psalm 119:133:
order my steps according to your word,
    and let not any iniquity have dominion over me.
Psalm 119:134:
deliver me from the oppression of man,
    so i will keep your precepts.
Psalm 119:135:
make your face to shine upon your servant,
    and teach me your statutes.
Psalm 119:136:
rivers of waters run down my eyes,
    because people do not keep your law.
Psalm 119:137:
you are righteous, o lord,
    and upright are your judgments.
Psalm 119:138:
you have set your testimonies in righteousness
    and faithfulness.
Psalm 119:139:
my zeal has consumed me,
    because my enemies have forgotten your words.
Psalm 119:140:
your word is pure and true;
    therefore your servant loves it.
Psalm 119:141:
i am small and despised,
    yet i do not forget your precepts.
Psalm 119:142:
your righteousness is an everlasting righteousness,
    and your law is true.
Psalm 119:143:
trouble and anguish have discovered me,
    but your commandments are my delight.
Psalm 119:144:
the righteousness of your testimonies is everlasting;
    grant me understanding, and i shall live.
Psalm 119:145:
i cried with my whole heart; hear me, o lord,
    i will keep your statutes.
Psalm 119:146:
i cried unto you; deliver me,
    and i shall keep your testimonies.
Psalm 119:147:
i arose before the dawn of the morning and cried for help;
    i hope in your words.
Psalm 119:148:
my eyes are awake before the night watches,
    that i might meditate on your word.
Psalm 119:149:
hear my voice according to your lovingkindness, o lord;
    revive me according to your judgment.
Psalm 119:150:
they draw close, those who persecute me with evil;
    they are far from your law.
Psalm 119:151:
but you are near, o lord,
    and all your commandments are true.
Psalm 119:152:
i have known of old
    that you have established your testimonies forever.
Psalm 119:153:
consider my affliction, and deliver me,
    for i do not forget your law.
Psalm 119:154:
plead my cause, and defend me;
    revive me according to your word.
Psalm 119:155:
salvation is far from the wicked,
    for they do not seek your statutes.
Psalm 119:156:
great are your compassions, o lord;
    revive me according to your judgments.
Psalm 119:157:
many are my persecutors and my enemies,
    yet i do not turn from your testimonies.
Psalm 119:158:
i behold the transgressors with disgust,
    because they have not kept your word.
Psalm 119:159:
consider how i love your precepts;
    revive me, o lord, according to your lovingkindness.
Psalm 119:160:
your word is true from the beginning,
    and every one of your righteous judgments endures forever.
Psalm 119:161:
princes have persecuted me without a cause,
    but my heart stands in awe of your words.
Psalm 119:162:
i rejoice at your word,
    as one who finds great plunder.
Psalm 119:163:
i hate and abhor lying,
    but i love your law.
Psalm 119:164:
seven times a day i praise you,
    because of your righteous judgments.
Psalm 119:165:
those who love your law have great peace,
    and nothing shall cause them to stumble.
Psalm 119:166:
lord, i have hoped for your deliverance,
    and i carry out your commandments.
Psalm 119:167:
my soul has kept your testimonies,
    and i love them greatly.
Psalm 119:168:
i have kept your precepts and your testimonies,
    for all my ways are before you.
Psalm 119:169:
let my cry come near before you, o lord;
    give me understanding according to your word.
Psalm 119:170:
let my supplication come before you;
    deliver me according to your word.
Psalm 119:171:
my lips shall declare praise,
    for you have taught me your statutes.
Psalm 119:172:
my tongue shall speak of your word,
    for all your commandments are right.
Psalm 119:173:
let your hand help me,
    for i have chosen your precepts.
Psalm 119:174:
i have longed for your salvation, o lord,
    and your law is my delight.
Psalm 119:175:
let my soul live and praise you,
    and let your judgments come to my aid.
Psalm 120:1:
in my distress i cried unto the lord,
    and he heard me.
Psalm 120:2:
deliver my soul, o lord, from lying lips
    and from a deceitful tongue.
Psalm 120:3:
what shall be given to you,
    or what shall be done to you, you false tongue?
Psalm 120:4:
sharp arrows of the warrior,
    with coals of the broom tree!
Psalm 120:5:
woe is me, that i have sojourned in meshek,
    or that i have dwelled among the tents of kedar!
Psalm 120:6:
my soul has long lived
    with those who hate peace.
Psalm 120:7:
i am for peace,
    but when i speak, they are for war!
Psalm 121:1:
i will lift up my eyes to the hills,
    from where does my help come?
Psalm 121:2:
my help comes from the lord,
    who made heaven and earth.
Psalm 121:3:
he will not let your foot slip;
    he who keeps you will not slumber.
Psalm 121:4:
behold, he who guards israel
    shall neither slumber nor sleep.
Psalm 121:5:
the lord is your guardian;
    the lord is your shade at your right hand.
Psalm 121:6:
the sun shall not harm you during the day,
    nor the moon during the night.
Psalm 121:7:
the lord shall protect you from all evil;
    he shall preserve your soul.
Psalm 121:8:
the lord shall preserve your going out and your coming in
    from now and for evermore.
Psalm 122:1:
i was glad when they said to me,
    “let us go into the house of the lord.”
Psalm 122:2:
our feet shall stand
    within your gates, o jerusalem.
Psalm 122:3:
jerusalem is built as a city
    that is designed for a multitude,
Psalm 122:4:
where the tribes go up,
    the tribes of the lord,
as a decree of israel,
    to give thanks unto the name of the lord.
Psalm 122:5:
there are set thrones of judgment,
    the thrones of the house of david.
Psalm 122:6:
pray for the peace of jerusalem:
    “may they prosper who love you!
Psalm 122:7:
peace be within your walls
    and security within your towers!”
Psalm 122:8:
for my brothers and companions’ sake,
    i will now say, “peace be within you.”
Psalm 122:9:
because of the house of the lord our god,
    i will seek your good.
Psalm 123:1:
to you i lift up my eyes,
    o you who dwell in the heavens.
Psalm 123:2:
behold, as the eyes of servants look to the hand of their master,
    and as the eyes of a maiden to the hand of her mistress,
so our eyes look upon the lord our god,
    until he has mercy upon us.
Psalm 123:3:
have mercy upon us, o lord, have mercy upon us,
    for we have been completely filled with contempt.
Psalm 123:4:
our soul is exceedingly filled with the ridicule of those who are at ease,
    and with the contempt of the proud ones.
Psalm 124:1:
if it had not been the lord who was on our side,
    now may israel say,
Psalm 124:2:
if it had not been the lord who was on our side,
    when men rose up against us,
Psalm 124:3:
then they would have swallowed us up,
    when their wrath was kindled against us;
Psalm 124:4:
then the flood would have overwhelmed us,
    the torrent would have passed over our lives;
Psalm 124:5:
then the surging waters
    would have gone over us.
Psalm 124:6:
blessed be the lord,
    who has not given us for a prey to their teeth.
Psalm 124:7:
we have escaped
    as a bird out of the snare of the hunters;
the snare is broken,
    and we have escaped.
Psalm 124:8:
our help is in the name of the lord,
    who made heaven and earth.
Psalm 125:1:
those who trust in the lord shall be as mount zion,
    which cannot be removed, but abides forever.
Psalm 125:2:
as the mountains are around jerusalem,
    so the lord surrounds his people,
    from now and forever.
Psalm 125:3:
for the scepter of the wicked shall not rest
    upon the land allotted to the righteous,
lest the righteous put forth
    their hands to do iniquity.
Psalm 125:4:
do good, o lord, for those who are good,
    and to those who are upright in their hearts.
Psalm 125:5:
as for those who turn aside to their twisted ways,
    the lord shall lead them away with the other workers of iniquity. 
peace be upon israel!
Psalm 126:1:
when the lord restored the captives of zion,
    we were like those who dream.
Psalm 126:2:
then our mouth was filled with laughter,
    and our tongue with singing.
then they said among the nations,
    “the lord has done great things for them.”
Psalm 126:3:
the lord has done great things for us;
    we are glad.
Psalm 126:4:
restore our captives, o lord,
    as the streams in the negev.
Psalm 126:5:
those who sow in tears
    shall reap in joy.
Psalm 126:6:
he who goes forth and weeps,
    bearing precious seed to sow,
shall come home again with rejoicing,
    bringing his grain sheaves with him.
Psalm 127:2:
it is in vain for you to rise up early,
    to stay up late,
and to eat the bread of hard toil,
    for he gives sleep to his beloved.
Psalm 127:3:
look, children are a gift of the lord,
    and the fruit of the womb is a reward.
Psalm 127:4:
as arrows in the hand of a mighty warrior,
    so are the children of one’s youth.
Psalm 127:5:
happy is the man
    who has his quiver full of them;
he shall not be ashamed
    when he speaks with the enemies at the gate.
Psalm 128:1:
blessed is everyone who fears the lord,
    who walks in his ways.
Psalm 128:2:
for you shall eat the fruit of the labor of your hands;
    you will be happy, and it shall be well with you.
Psalm 128:3:
your wife shall be as a fruitful vine
    in your house,
your children like olive shoots
    around your table.
Psalm 128:4:
behold, this man shall be blessed
    who fears the lord.
Psalm 128:5:
the lord shall bless you from zion,
    and may you see the welfare of jerusalem
all the days of your life.
Psalm 128:6:
indeed, may you see your children’s children.
peace upon israel!
Psalm 129:1:
“often they have afflicted me from my youth,”
    may israel now say,
Psalm 129:2:
“often they have afflicted me from my youth,
    yet they have not prevailed against me.
Psalm 129:3:
the plowmen plowed upon my back;
    they made their furrows long.”
Psalm 129:4:
the lord is righteous;
    he has cut the cords of the wicked.
Psalm 129:5:
let all those be shamed
    and turned back who hate zion.
Psalm 129:6:
let them be as the grass on the housetops,
    which withers before it even grows,
Psalm 129:7:
where the reaper is unable to fill his hand,
    or he who binds sheaves, his arms.
Psalm 130:1: from the depths i call on you, o lord!
Psalm 130:3:
if you, o lord, should keep track of iniquities,
    o lord, who shall stand?
Psalm 130:4:
for there is forgiveness with you,
    that you may be feared.
Psalm 130:5:
i wait for the lord, with bated breath i wait;
    i long for his word!
Psalm 130:6:
my soul waits for the lord,
    more than watchmen for the morning,
    more than watchmen for the morning.
Psalm 130:8:
he shall redeem israel
    from all their iniquities.
Psalm 131:1:
lord, my heart is not haughty,
    my eyes are not raised too high.
i have not striven for enormities,
    for things too wonderful for me.
Psalm 131:3:
let israel hope in the lord
    from now and forever.
Psalm 132:1:
o lord, remember david
    and all his afflictions,
Psalm 132:2:
how he swore unto the lord,
    and vowed unto the mighty god of jacob:
Psalm 132:3:
“i will not come into my house,
    nor go up to my bed;
Psalm 132:4:
i will not give sleep to my eyes,
    or slumber to my eyelids,
Psalm 132:5:
until i find a place for the lord,
    a dwelling for the mighty god of jacob.”
Psalm 132:6:
we heard of it in ephrathah;
    we found it in the fields of jaar.
Psalm 132:7:
“we will go to his dwelling place,
    we will worship at his footstool.”
Psalm 132:8:
arise, o lord, go to your resting place,
    you and the ark of your strength.
Psalm 132:9:
let your priests be clothed with righteousness,
    and let your godly ones shout for joy.
Psalm 132:10:
for your servant david’s sake,
    do not turn away your anointed king.
Psalm 132:11:
the lord has sworn with a sure oath to david
    that he will not turn from it:
“from the fruit of your body
    i will set a son on your throne.
Psalm 132:12:
if your children will keep my covenant
    and my testimonies that i shall teach them,
then their children shall also sit
    upon your throne forever.”
Psalm 132:13:
for the lord has chosen zion;
    he has desired it for his dwelling:
Psalm 132:14:
“this is my resting place forever;
    here i will dwell, for i have chosen it.
Psalm 132:15:
i will abundantly bless her provisions;
    i will satisfy her poor with bread.
Psalm 132:16:
i will also clothe her priests with salvation,
    and her godly ones shall shout for joy.
Psalm 132:17:
“there i will make a horn sprout for david;
    i have prepared a lamp for my anointed one.
Psalm 132:18:
his enemies i will clothe with shame,

Psalm 138:1:

Psalm 139:1:
o lord, you have searched me
    and known me.
Psalm 139:2:
you know when i sit down and when i get up;
    you understand my thought from far off.
Psalm 139:3:
you search my path and my lying down
    and are aware of all my ways.
Psalm 139:4:
for there is not a word on my tongue,
    but behold, o lord, you know it fully.
Psalm 139:5:
you put yourself behind and before me,
    and keep your hand on me.
Psalm 139:6:
such knowledge is too wonderful for me;
    it is lofty, and i cannot fathom it.
Psalm 139:7:
where shall i go from your spirit,
    or where shall i flee from your presence?
Psalm 139:8:
if i ascend to heaven, you are there;
    if i make my bed in sheol, you are there.
Psalm 139:9:
if i take the wings of the morning
    and dwell at the end of the sea,
Psalm 139:10:
even there your hand shall guide me,

Psalm 139:11:
if i say, “surely the darkness shall cover me,
    and the light shall be as night about me,”

even the darkness is not dark to you,

    for the darkness is like light to you.
Psalm 139:13:
you brought my inner parts into being;

Psalm 139:15:
my frame was not hidden from you
    when i was made in secret,

Psalm 139:16:
your eyes saw me unformed,
yet in your book

    before any of them came into being.
Psalm 139:17:

Psalm 139:23:
search me, o god, and know my heart;

man is like a breath;

whose mouth speaks lies,

    and i will praise your name forever and ever.

great is the lord, and greatly to be praised,

one generation shall praise your works to another

i will speak of the glorious honor of your majesty
    and of your wondrous works.

they shall speak of the might of your awesome acts,
    and i will declare your greatness.
Psalm 145:7:
they shall abundantly declare the fame of your great goodness
    and shall sing of your righteousness.

the lord is gracious and full of compassion,
    slow to anger, and great in mercy.

the lord is good to all,
    and his compassion is over all his works.

all your works shall praise you, o lord,
    and your godly ones shall bless you.

they shall speak of the glory of your kingdom
    and talk of your power,

Psalm 145:13:
your kingdom is an everlasting kingdom,
    and your dominion endures throughout all generations.
Psalm 145:14:
the lord upholds all who fall,
    and raises up all who are bowed down.
Psalm 145:15:
the eyes of all wait upon you,
    and you give them their food in due season.
Psalm 145:16:
you open your hand
    and satisfy the desire of every living thing.
Psalm 145:17:
the lord is righteous in all his ways
    and loving in all his works.
Psalm 145:18:
the lord is near to all those who call upon him,
    to all who call upon him in truth.
Psalm 145:19:
he will fulfill the desire of those who fear him;
    he also will hear their cry and will save them.
Psalm 145:20:
the lord preserves all those who love him,
    but all the wicked he will destroy.
Psalm 145:21:
my mouth shall speak the praise of the lord,
    and let all people bless his holy name
    forever and ever.

to know wisdom and instruction,
    to perceive the words of understanding,
Proverbs 1:3:
to receive the instruction of wisdom,
    justice, judgment, and equity;
Proverbs 1:4:
to give subtlety to the simple,
    to the young man knowledge and discretion—
Proverbs 1:5:
a wise man will hear and will increase learning,
    and a man of understanding will attain wise counsel,
Proverbs 1:6:
to understand a proverb and the interpretation,
    the words of the wise and their riddles.
Proverbs 1:7:
the fear of the lord is the beginning of knowledge,
    but fools despise wisdom and instruction.
Proverbs 1:8:
my son, hear the instruction of your father,
